response.markdown_report:
### Insights and directions

**Starting point.** (1) Users report stale-interest revival and weak connections to current intent. Emphasizing recent next-item decisions is a plausible response, but training-loss weighting does not directly control inference-time forgetting. (2) Electronics has the weakest measured separation: 9.7% wrong-order comparisons and a 0.0265 tenth-percentile margin. Competitive negatives therefore offer a targeted optimization hypothesis. (3) Collapse scores around 0.5 imply mean cosine similarity near zero. They do not justify embedding-diversity regularization, and sampled margins do not establish validation gains.

**Related work.** (1) [GRU4Rec’s ranking-loss study](https://hidasi.eu/assets/pdf/gru4rec_v2_cikm18.pdf) motivates BPR-max because easy negatives dilute ranking gradients. Its [official implementation](https://github.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec_PyTorch_Official/blob/master/gru4rec_pytorch.py) specifies differentiable negative-score weights and score regularization. (2) [Recency-biased sampling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02643) supports emphasizing recent targets, while [TiCoSeRec](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/25540) motivates using interaction intervals. Neither establishes that positional loss weighting reduces stale recommendations. (3) [UFNRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04116) identifies false-negative risks; observed-history exclusions cannot remove all plausible but unobserved positives.

### Framework and candidates

Three directions remain: **intent emphasis** changes which training positions matter; **ranking discrimination** changes which competitors matter; **semantic specificity** changes item representations. Training recency, timestamp recency and inference-time history retention are distinct interventions.

Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/implementation difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder. Alignment measures hypothesized relevance, not demonstrated benefit.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. Recency-weighted BPR-max | 3/6/6/8/4 | Feasible combination targets recent decisions and confusing competitors | Established components; staleness mechanism remains indirect; exclusions add engineering work |
| B. Prefix-gap-conditioned GRU retention, inspired by TiCoSeRec | 5/7/8/5/6 | More directly changes retention of potentially stale interests | Time-aware GRUs have precedents; gaps can reflect purchase frequency rather than preference change |
| C. Joint title-token and ID embeddings, inspired by [Recformer](https://cseweb.ucsd.edu/~jmcauley/pdfs/kdd23b.pdf) | 4/6/7/6/6 | Shares specific textual evidence across sparse items | Broad lexical similarity may reproduce observed errors; text does not establish compatibility |

### Selected experiment: recency-weighted BPR-max

At 0% progress, retain **A** for feasibility. It explicitly targets **revived older interests** through recent-target emphasis and **weakly connected items displacing immediate matches** through competitive-negative training. These are hypotheses; neither incompatibility nor redundant ownership is directly supervised.

For each valid position, sample 32 uniform negatives with replacement, excluding padding, its target and the user’s training-observed items. This deliberately differs from official GRU4Rec sampling. Compute `−log Σ softmax(negative_score)·sigmoid(positive_score−negative_score)` plus `0.001·Σ softmax(negative_score)·negative_score²`; differentiate through both softmax terms. Weight positions by `0.5 + 0.5*exp(−distance/10)` and normalize over valid targets. Anchor distance to the final training target in the complete training history, including when sampling earlier crops.

Run a minimal factorial comparison: baseline loss/BPR-max × uniform/positional weighting. Keep architecture, batches, optimizer, negative draws where applicable, evaluation schedule and epoch budget matched. This separates objective and weighting effects; defer timestamp weighting and retention changes until justified. Inspect Electronics’ lower-tail margins, category results and history-length strata. HR@10 alone cannot demonstrate reduced staleness.

Preserve seed 42, preprocessing seed 0, at most 200 epochs, 200 batches/epoch, four routes, `os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']`, trial-local artifacts and one checkpoint/category. Keep diagnostic interfaces and final-nonpadding readout. The predictor writer must reproduce the trained architecture. Use fixed macro validation HR@10; record all trials and, when per-user hits are available, report a category-stratified paired bootstrap interval. Each additional hit changes macro HR by 0.00125. Intervals remain conditional on fixed candidates and do not correct adaptive selection; gains concern the pinned 100-candidate protocol, not full-catalog ranking.

idea.description: Train the corrected GRU4Rec with recency-weighted BPR-max, using a modest negative pool and one independently trained model per category. Separate the contributions of ranking loss and positional weighting through controlled comparisons.
idea.motivation: Target stale-interest revival and weakly connected recommendations while improving the weak positive-negative separation measured especially in Electronics. Recent-target emphasis changes learning priorities rather than directly enforcing inference-time forgetting; competitive negatives improve discrimination without establishing compatibility. These mechanisms remain hypotheses. Fixed macro validation HR@10 determines selection, while sampled margins and qualitative rejection patterns provide supporting diagnostics.
idea.implementation_notes:
Keep the supplied corrected GRU architecture, optimizer configuration, dropout, batch size, sequence length, score transformation and prediction function unchanged for the initial comparison; record their resolved values from the supplied baseline rather than inventing replacements. Preserve the baseline's preprocessing, splits, routing and evaluation schedule. Use preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per epoch. Keep DATA_DIR as os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], all artifacts beneath the trial directory, and single-GPU execution. Each deployed category loads exactly one selected checkpoint; experimental variants are never combined or averaged.

For each valid training target, draw 32 item IDs uniformly with replacement from catalog IDs excluding padding, the target and every item in that user's complete training history. Do not consult validation or test labels for exclusions. Repeated negative IDs are permitted. Implement exclusions using cached training-history membership and rejection sampling; handle an empty eligible catalog explicitly by omitting that position and recording its count. Vectorize or chunk scoring as necessary to respect GPU memory. This sampler is a deliberate deviation from official GRU4Rec's minibatch targets plus shared popularity-adjustable pool; it is not a reproduction of that sampling procedure. Do not apply logQ correction to BPR-max.

Compute BPR-max using log_softmax over negative scores and logsumexp of weighted log-sigmoid preferences. This is the negative log of a weighted probability sum, not the weighted average of log losses. Add coefficient 0.001 times the softmax-weighted squared negative scores. Do not detach softmax weights. Retain the baseline score parameterization rather than silently adding the official implementation's optional ELU transformation.

For the target at absolute zero-based training-history index t, define distance as T-1-t, where T is that user's full training-history length. Apply weight 0.5 + 0.5*exp(-distance/10). Carry absolute target indices from the internal sampler when cropping histories; never treat every sampled crop endpoint as the latest user interaction. Normalize the summed loss by the summed weights over valid targets. Uniform weighting is exactly weight=1. Long histories may have most targets near the 0.5 floor; inspect effective weighting by history length before attributing behavior to recency.

Use four controlled configurations: unchanged baseline objective with uniform weights; unchanged baseline objective with positional weights; BPR-max with uniform weights; BPR-max with positional weights. Hold negative IDs fixed between the two BPR-max weighting variants using a dedicated seeded sampling generator. If the baseline objective cannot consume the same negative pool without changing its definition, document that the objective comparison includes a sampling change. Keep batch streams, initialization, evaluation cadence, checkpoint tie-breaking and maximum training budgets consistent. Reserve budget for all four categories; do not launch comparisons whose conservative projected cost exceeds the remaining 43,200 GPU-second allowance. Record incomplete and failed trials. Defer additional decay sweeps, timestamp weighting and architectural retention changes until these comparisons justify their cost.

Preserve family-specific sample_batch and ModelView compatibility: item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data. If absolute target indices are needed internally, keep them outside the public diagnosis-loader tuple, which remains (None, sequence, positive, negative) with B x L tensors. DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader) must return measured metrics and metric_definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis) must retain the measured values and definitions. Use only public histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps. Leave category breakdowns unavailable when category metadata is absent; do not infer ratings, reviews, compatibility labels or simulator traits. Use identical diagnostic examples and negatives across comparisons where possible. Distinguish changes caused by score scale from changes in wrong-order rates.

For left-padded inference histories, gather the largest position index whose item ID is nonzero, never nonpadding_count-1; preserve the corrected baseline's handling of empty histories. Keep the embedded predictor writer consistent with the trained architecture and score transformation. Any inference change requires updating that writer in the same change.

Select configurations using the fixed four-category macro validation HR@10 and the host's pinned 200-user/category, 99-unique-negative protocol. Retain the existing checkpoint-selection rule and evaluation cadence; do not increase validation frequency for favored variants. When the host exposes paired user hit indicators, estimate uncertainty with 10,000 category-stratified paired bootstrap resamples using a separate analysis RNG seeded 42; average category differences equally and report percentile 95% intervals. Do not modify the evaluator to obtain unavailable outputs. These intervals condition on fitted models and fixed candidates, omit training/candidate randomness and do not correct adaptive model selection. Record all comparisons, interpret small gains provisionally, and leave hidden test information entirely outside search. Qualitative evidence from the same twenty training users can assess stated mechanisms, but it is neither an independent generalization estimate nor a replacement selection metric.
idea.pseudocode:
configs = [(baseline_loss, uniform), (baseline_loss, positional),
           (bpr_max, uniform), (bpr_max, positional)]
for config in budget_feasible_configs(configs):
    for category in four_categories:
        reset_training_seed(42)
        model = corrected_GRU4Rec_with_inherited_configuration()
        for epoch in range(max_epochs_at_most_200):
            for step in range(200):
                batch = internal_family_sample_batch_with_absolute_target_indices()
                sequence, positive = batch.sequence, batch.positive
                features = model.log2feats(sequence)
                valid = (sequence != 0) & (positive != 0)
                distance = batch.full_training_length[:, None] - 1 - batch.target_index
                weight = ones_like(positive, float)
                if config.weighting == positional:
                    weight = 0.5 + 0.5 * exp(-clamp_min(distance, 0) / 10)
                if config.objective == bpr_max:
                    negatives, eligible = sample_uniform_with_replacement(
                        users=batch.users, K=32,
                        exclude=complete_training_history_plus_target_and_padding)
                    valid = valid & eligible
                    pos_score = model.predict_score(features, positive)
                    neg_score = score_K_items_with_same_model(features, negatives)
                    log_weight = log_softmax(neg_score, dim=-1)
                    log_preference = logsigmoid(pos_score[..., None] - neg_score)
                    rank_loss = -logsumexp(log_weight + log_preference, dim=-1)
                    regularizer = 0.001 * sum(exp(log_weight) * neg_score.square(), dim=-1)
                    per_position_loss = rank_loss + regularizer
                else:
                    per_position_loss = unchanged_baseline_unreduced_loss(batch, features)
                effective_weight = weight * valid
                if sum(effective_weight) > 0:
                    loss = sum(effective_weight * per_position_loss) / sum(effective_weight)
                    optimizer_step(loss)
            evaluate_at_inherited_validation_cadence()
        retain_one_checkpoint_using_inherited_selection_rule(category)
    compare_fixed_four_category_macro_validation_HR10()
select_one_configuration_without_score_fusion()
write_predictor_matching_selected_GRU_architecture_and_scoring()
# Inference readout: largest index with sequence != 0; preserve empty-row handling.
# Public diagnosis loader remains (None, sequence, positive, negative).

originality.positive: The diagnosis-driven combination of bounded positional weighting, conservative exclusions and GRU ranking optimization forms a clear constrained experiment.
originality.negative: BPR-max and recency-aware training are established; no new architecture, objective principle or demonstrated mechanism is introduced.

future_potential.positive: Factorial comparisons can identify whether target emphasis and competitive negatives offer a useful foundation for later time-aware GRU retention.
future_potential.negative: Positional weighting may have limited influence on current intent, and sparse validation gains may not transfer across categories or candidate protocols.

code_difficulty.positive: The initial proposal preserves the GRU backbone and inference architecture, concentrating changes in training loss and sampling.
code_difficulty.negative: Efficient user-specific exclusions, absolute target indices for cropped histories, unreduced baseline losses and controlled sampling streams require careful implementation.

related_work.title: Recurrent Neural Networks with Top-k Gains for Session-based Recommendations
contributions: Introduces ranking objectives including BPR-max that emphasize competitive negatives.
Provides an objective directly compatible with a GRU4Rec backbone.
limitations: Does not establish improvements on the pinned four-category RecHarness benchmark.
Does not directly resolve current-intent drift or product compatibility.

related_work.title: Official GRU4Rec PyTorch implementation
contributions: Specifies BPR-max with differentiable negative-score softmax weights and negative-score regularization.
Documents minibatch-target and shared additional-negative sampling, including its masking behavior.
limitations: The proposed history-excluding uniform sampler deliberately differs from the official procedure.
Implementation details such as optional ELU scoring and reduction conventions must be specified rather than assumed.

related_work.title: TiCoSeRec
contributions: Uses interaction intervals to motivate time-aware sequence augmentation and preference modeling.
limitations: Does not validate the proposed positional recency weighting.
Its temporal augmentation is distinct from a GRU retention mechanism.

related_work.title: Recency-biased Sampling for Training Sequential Recommenders
contributions: Studies recency-biased positive sampling and reports effectiveness improvements including for GRU4Rec.
Provides precedent for changing training emphasis toward recent targets.
limitations: Changes target sampling rather than directly validating the proposed bounded loss weights.
Does not establish reduced stale-interest recommendations in this benchmark.

related_work.title: UFNRec
contributions: Studies false negatives in sequential recommendation, motivating caution with aggressive negative mining.
limitations: Observed-history exclusion cannot eliminate all false negatives.
Does not determine the best negative-pool size for this benchmark.

related_work.title: Recformer
contributions: Combines textual item understanding with recommendation learning.
Motivates semantic representations as a possible direction for sparse items.
limitations: Its language-model architecture and training setting do not establish benefits for a randomly initialized GRU text encoder.
Textual similarity alone does not establish complementarity or compatibility.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled recommendation metrics can reverse model comparisons.
Supports interpreting results specifically under the pinned candidate protocol.
limitations: Does not justify changing the host evaluator.
Does not imply that this experiment's observed comparison will necessarily reverse under full-catalog evaluation.

related_work.title: SciPy bootstrap documentation
contributions: Documents paired bootstrap resampling principles applicable to aligned user outcomes.
limitations: Category-stratified macro comparisons require preserving the benchmark's equal category weighting.
Ordinary paired intervals do not capture adaptive selection bias, training randomness or candidate-resampling uncertainty.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains how optimization over noisy validation estimates can produce substantial selection bias.
Motivates restrained comparisons and complete trial accounting.
limitations: Does not provide a correction specific to this small fixed RecHarness validation set.
Post-selection bootstrap intervals alone do not resolve the problem.
